author: v230_audit_runtime

historicalFailure.case: a definitive shared probe rejection releases capacity and is not cached
historicalFailure.primary: The old bare process.kill(previous.pid, 0) assertion did not throw after a successor had started.
historicalFailure.secondary: The unobserved retry promise was rejected by afterEach service.close, producing one unhandled runtime_lost rejection.
historicalFailure.limitation: The CI log contains neither original creation times nor retained process handles; it does not establish that the number was reused, nor that the original child survived.

diagnosis.classification: Test process-identity observation and delayed rejection-handler defects; no production cleanup defect found.
productionContract: Windows controller owns the child through a process handle and non-breakaway Job Object; TerminateJobObject is followed by active==0 and relay joins before success.
NativeRpc.close waits for the controller close and requires its exitCode to be 0; missing acknowledgement rejects.
probeDefaults awaits close in both normal completion and finally before the shared flight completes and capacity can start a successor.

details: Capture Windows creation time while the fixture is held; subsequent checks reject the same PID plus creation-time identity, while a reused numeric PID is distinct.
Keep invariant-culture UTC DateTime ticks as decimal text (100 ns representation); never convert them to a JavaScript Number. Each query uses a new Process object and disposes it.

Only GetProcessById ArgumentException (absent PID) becomes null; start-time lookup, access/query failure, malformed output, timeout and launcher error reject. Non-Windows preserves signal-0 observation and accepts only ESRCH as absent.
Observe each pending read immediately without replacing the original rejecting promise; replace the extra rejecting finally chain with two fulfilled settlement handlers.
Retain real process exit assertions, all shared cache/capacity/generation/retry assertions, and existing unknown-outcome cleanup guards. No production edits or sleeps/retries added.

newMeaningfulChecks: Repeated observations of the held process return the identical creation-time string; the stop guard rejects that still-live predecessor.
Actual close makes the captured predecessor identity disappear; after an event-loop turn the original request still rejects with runtime_lost/unknown without an unhandled error.
A real Windows query of an absent PID returns null; an out-of-Int32 query error rejects instead of becoming absent.
The original retry-after-definitive-rejection case passes; the Windows Job ownership suite passes, including detached descendants, backpressure, owner death and unacknowledged controller failure.

limits: This is targeted Windows verification, not a new full-suite pass; CI5 remains historically failed.
The failure was not reproduced with retained historical process identity; PID reuse is a possibility, not a proven historical event.
No actual access-denied process query was forced. Its fail-closed branch was inspected; an actual other query error was exercised.
No Linux rerun was performed for this Windows-specific identity repair; the non-Windows liveness mechanism is unchanged.
No commit, CI trigger, network request, deployment, credentials or inference performed.
